entities.name: Thirsty Desert
entities.summary: Stony waste in ridges like sea waves, crusted with salt, with small sage bushes; full of the dried dead of many ages.

refs.q: a stony waste like unto that which they had passed through before they came to the House of the Sorceress, save that this lay in ridges as the waves of a great sea
the face of the wilderness was covered with a salt scurf, and that naught grew there save a sprinkling of small sage bushes

entities.name: (unnamed) dead of the Thirsty Desert
entities.summary: Dried corpses of many ages and fashions of armour, including women; none wear the beads.

refs.q: their raiment and wargear both, is of many fashions, and some much more perished than other

spatial.travel_time_text: wood ends on the third day

refs.q: on the third day they came to where it thinned and at last died out into a stony waste

travel.duration_text: three days in the wood, then three or more days in the desert

refs.q: They lived well while they were in the wood

facts.subject: (unnamed) woodland of the Sorceress
facts.statement: Wild creatures there know no man and are tame; a robin perches on Ursula's wrist.

refs.q: in that wood most of the creatures, knowing not man, were tame to him

facts.subject: Thirsty Desert
facts.statement: In the dry salt waste the dead dry like leather without rotting.

refs.q: in the saltness of the dry desert the flesh had dried on his bones without corrupting, and was as hardened leather

facts.subject: Thirsty Desert
facts.statement: Seekers must cross the ridges at their highest to avoid a maze of hills leading nowhere.

refs.q: these same ridges they were bidden to cross over at their highest, lest they should be bewildered in a maze of little hills and dales leading no whither

facts.subject: Thirsty Desert
facts.statement: The dead came over a long time, one, two or three at a time.

refs.q: this army of dead men has not come all in one day or one year, but in a long, long while

facts.subject: Well at the World's End
facts.statement: None of the desert's dead wear the seekers' beads.

refs.q: ever and anon they looked to them to note if they wore the beads like to them but saw none so dight

events.label: Crossing the Thirsty Desert
events.summary: The lovers cross the salt ridges among the dried dead, burying some.

refs.q: Ralph and Ursula buried these two with the heaping of stones

unresolved.question: Why the dead died: thirst, the Dry Tree's poison, or failure without the beads. Not stated here.

refs.q: would not the Sage or his books have told us of the most deadly?

opportunities.idea: A desert of the dead as a hazard zone with environmental storytelling (gear from many eras).

basis_refs.q: their raiment and wargear both, is of many fashions

ledger.summary: In the wood past the House the lovers rest under an oak; Ralph fears loneliness in a long life; a tame robin perches on Ursula's wrist, the wood's creatures being tame. After three days the wood ends in a stony waste in wave-like ridges, to be crossed at their highest points, covered with salt scurf and small sage bushes. On the second day they find a dried, unwounded armoured corpse, horses, and a woman who stabbed herself, and bury them under stones; then more dead. On the third day there are too many to bury. Ursula notes none wear the seekers' beads, the dead are from many ages, and the way-tokens still show; they go on.
ledger.geography_notes: Past the House: wildwood for three days, thinning to a stony waste in long ridges like sea waves, salt-crusted, with small sage bushes. Ridges must be crossed at their highest to avoid a maze of little hills and dales. A last clear brook before the desert. Dead seekers lie along the ridges; the way-token is seen on rocks.
